title: Cap. VI Arg. 4: Augustine John 6:45 — special vocation implies antecedent will to save
pass_a_gloss: So Augustine, disputing of the predestined and the passed-by from that place, Everyone who has heard from the Father, and has learned, comes to me, John 6:45: All these, he says, God teaches to come to Christ, all these he wills to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For if he had also willed to teach those for whom the word of the Cross is foolishness, that they might come to Christ, without doubt they also would have come. In this special vocation therefore we must necessarily acknowledge a special and antecedent will of saving those so called.
pass_b_english: So Augustine on the predestined and the passed-by, from John 6:45 (Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me): all these God teaches to come to Christ; all these he wills saved and brought to the knowledge of the truth. Had he also willed to teach those for whom the Cross is foolishness to come to Christ, they too would have come. In this special vocation, then, we must grant a special antecedent will to save those so called.
source_text: Sic Augustinus de praedestinatis et praeteritis disputans ex illo loco, Omnis qui audivit a Patre, et didicit, venit ad me, Joann. vi. 45: Hos omnes, inquit, docet venire ad Christum Deus, hos omnes vult salvos fieri, et in agnitionem veritatis venire. Nam si illos etiam, quibus stultitia est verbum Crucis, ut ad Christum venirent, docere voluisset, proculdubio venirent et ipsi. In hac igitur speciali vocatione agnoscamus necesse est specialem et antecedentem voluntatem salvandi sic vocatos.
